ctx.x: You know I find with the college, the young students I'm working with, they go out, take their gigs and play their things. I find that they get so involved in learning the latest hit jazz tunes that they don't have any repertoire. I've even tried to take them, like at Christmas holiday time I took them to (unintelligible) 's school and the teachers. And, you know, they're learning songs.

Well, even the big jazz players now. You know what happens is they're playing these what they call modal tunes, they've only got two goddamned chords for 20 minutes. And that's what they're copying, songs with two chords. And that's why they don't know how to get -- and they complain, they say at Berkeley all they teach us is 2-5-1. I say, well, you need a lot more 2-5-1 because all you play is 1. You've got to get there, but they don't because all music is 2-5-1. Even Beethoven is 2-5-1.

Sure, I tell them, you're limiting yourself. You've got to learn these songs, and especially if you're a New York musician, if you expect to make a living in New York, you've got to know your instrument. If you can't get in a studio, you're going to have to take a club date. And you should also have you a Broadway show book and learn the tunes of a Broadway show.
